clue.text: Cook sounds like an ass, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word is judged by how it is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: a donkey's cry is a bray, so its noises are brays

explanation.surface: A clumsy cook who apparently sounds like a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' is not the homophone signal here: it is part of the description of a donkey's noise; 'we hear' does the sound work.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook slowly in a little liquid in a closed pot.

clue.text: Damned bishop didn't run out

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
supplies that did not run out lasted

explanation.surface: A cursed bishop who somehow never ran out of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasted is a mild curse word, a softened equivalent of damned as an intensifier.

clue.text: Decorate sailors after fuss

indicators.note: after places the fuss first and the sailors following it, so the pieces join in the reverse of their printed order

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
RN is the Royal Navy, the usual crossword source of sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors brought in to dress up a ship once the fuss has died down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the sailors second, following the fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn something is to decorate or embellish it with ornaments.

clue.text: Observe woodwork going up and down

blocks.note: to observe is to see
sawing is a typical bit of woodwork

explanation.surface: Watching a carpenter whose saw keeps moving up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Seesawing describes alternating motion, rising and falling like a playground plank.

clue.text: Have faith in cover held back by worker

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end towards its start
something held is gripped inside something else, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the worker bee is the crossword's stock worker
a veil covers the face

explanation.surface: A worker trusts a cover story that is being withheld.
explanation.walkthrough: The cover word is turned round and then placed inside the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To believe is to trust or accept as true, exactly having faith in someone.

clue.text: Birds used big nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters beside it have gone wild and are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Some birds have eaten large nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' reads as food for the birds, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Budgies, short for budgerigars, are small Australian parakeets often kept as pets.

clue.text: McCartney from Liverpool in dancehall

indicators.note: coming from the words means the letters are lifted out of the run of text

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A McCartney from Liverpool spotted in a dancehall.
explanation.walkthrough: Linda McCartney, photographer and Paul McCartney's first wife, was actually American, so the Liverpool link is part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda McCartney is a well-known bearer of the surname, so her first name stands for it.

clue.text: New deal with China to supply spicy food

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters of both words; 'with' joins them

explanation.surface: A fresh trade deal with China to supply spicy food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two words of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican rolled tortilla with a filling and chilli sauce.

clue.text: Still getting letters from Stevenson

indicators.note: getting letters from a name means taking a consecutive run of them out of it

blocks.note: a run of letters inside the surname

explanation.surface: Someone still receives letters from the writer Stevenson.
explanation.definitionFit: Still as a sentence adverb means nevertheless, which is what even so means.

clue.text: College grounds affected American

blocks.note: camp means theatrically affected or exaggerated
US abbreviates the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: The college grounds have influenced an American student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like a verb meaning influenced; it is the adjective meaning mannered.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the site and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Safe radio broadcast, as previously mentioned

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread and regathered

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cautious radio programme, as was noted earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid is a formal, legal-sounding word for something referred to earlier.

clue.text: Hours in pleasant alcove

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for hours

explanation.surface: Spending hours relaxing in a pleasant nook.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a shallow recess in a wall, the same as an alcove.

clue.text: Silver not from the right South Pacific country

indicators.note: reading from the right means going against normal order, from the end back to the start

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written

explanation.surface: Silver that did not come from the political right in a Pacific nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not from the right' wants to read as a deletion or a politics remark; 'not' is a piece and 'from the right' reverses both.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is an island kingdom in Polynesia, in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Proper sign for US elections

blocks.note: prim means proper and formal
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A correct signal given for American polls.
explanation.definitionFit: Primaries are preliminary votes in which US parties choose their candidates.

clue.text: Welshman doesn't tell the truth in newspapers

blocks.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, a crossword stock Welshman
someone who does not tell the truth lies

explanation.surface: A Welshman is caught lying in the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dailies are newspapers published every day.

clue.text: Location of groundsheet upset no one? That's the aim

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down clue that sends the letters back up the column

blocks.note: a groundsheet lies in a tent
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A camper's groundsheet has bothered nobody, which was the whole point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No one' looks like a single idea, nobody; it splits into two pieces that are then turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is a purpose or plan, the thing one aims to achieve.

clue.text: Lust worried an eastern ruler

indicators.note: worried can mean shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Desire troubled a ruler in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' reads as the ruler's anxiety, but it scrambles the letters either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is a Muslim sovereign, a ruler typical of the historic Middle East.

clue.text: As to clues being cracked, it's a hopeless endeavour

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the letters fall into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A solver says that working out these clues is futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' looks like solving the clues, as solvers say; here it means broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is an effort or movement with no chance of success.

clue.text: Greek letter about end of bailout is a disgrace

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept
about means around, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: sigma is the Greek S
its final letter

explanation.surface: A financial rescue package is condemned as shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame or disgrace attached to someone.

clue.text: Ordering caviare demonstrates greed

indicators.note: ordering means arranging, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Asking for caviar in a restaurant shows a greedy streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordering' reads as asking for food in a restaurant; it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is extreme desire for wealth, a synonym of greed.

clue.text: Lose hope when changing diapers

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A weary parent losing hope while changing a baby's nappies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' fits the nappies so well that it hides its job as the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to give up all hope, a verb matching lose hope.

clue.text: Pass over pages on English or French port

blocks.note: to pass over, as a euphemism, is to die
pp is the abbreviation for pages
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Skipping some pages on English or French in a textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the pages above English in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a ferry port on the Normandy coast of northern France.

clue.text: Akin, so it is said

blocks.note: first meaning: connected by family or kind
second meaning: told or narrated, as a story is

explanation.surface: Two things are similar, or so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So it is said' sounds like a hedge on the first part; it is a second meaning, a story having been recounted.
explanation.definitionFit: Related means connected by kinship, and is also the past participle of relate, to recount.

clue.text: What Guevara's masseur provided for angel?

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
a masseur gives a rub

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what a revolutionary's masseur gave an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase, a rub for Che is a Che rub, which joins up into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a type of angel, often pictured as a chubby winged child.

clue.text: Greeting crew members with fish

blocks.note: a ship's crew members are hands
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Sailors greet each other while holding fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A handshake is a greeting made by clasping another person's hand.

clue.text: Female graduate in old queen's place

blocks.note: she is the female pronoun
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A female graduate living where an ancient queen once lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba is the biblical kingdom ruled by the Queen of Sheba, who visited Solomon.

clue.text: After central heating I'll cool off

blocks.note: CH is the estate agent's abbreviation for central heating
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Once the heating is on, someone promises to stop being hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the second piece after the heating; the apostrophe in I'll is ignored, as punctuation usually is.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill is to become cold or to relax, matching cooling off in both senses.

clue.text: Perfect croupier's job description?

blocks.note: first meaning: as good as it could be
second meaning, read cryptically: what a card dealer would say of the job, split as two words

explanation.walkthrough: A croupier deals cards, so the job is summed up as 'I deal'; the question mark warns that the second reading is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means perfect, the best that could be imagined.

clue.text: Thick-skinned beast dropping back by European river

indicators.note: dropping the back of a word means losing its final letter

blocks.note: a rhinoceros has notably thick skin
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A rhino retreating beside a European river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major river flowing from the Alps through Germany to the North Sea.

clue.text: Cheeky about Russian leader? That's unwise!

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is kept
about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: impudent means cheeky or insolent
its first letter

explanation.surface: Being rude about the Kremlin's boss is a risky move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian leader' suggests a president's name; it means only the first letter of Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means lacking prudence or care, so rash and unwise.

clue.text: Group taking long time dressing

blocks.note: a band is a group, of musicians or people
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A pop group spends ages getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' looks like putting clothes on; it is the covering for a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material used to dress a wound.

clue.text: He ordered lead and made well

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man in charge gave instructions and cured someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as giving commands; it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Healed is the past tense of heal, to restore to health, so cured.
